signal_rationale.delta: By October 2026, evidence from labour markets, software valuations, pricing models, cloud regulation and energy infrastructure can be connected into one observable shift: AI is reducing the scarcity of some cognitive tasks and application features while raising the strategic scarcity of compute, power, capital, distribution and trusted workflows.
signal_rationale.evidence: The assessment triangulates Stanford labour and investment data, ILO and OECD occupational exposure, NBER and METR productivity evidence, SEG and Stripe software-market data, Salesforce pricing, IEA physical-infrastructure data, FTC and European Commission competition work, Microsoft filings and clearly labelled investor theses.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Further diffusion depends on lower model and inference costs, reliable agentic workflows and organizational redesign; concentration depends on whether chips, electricity, grid access, cloud, proprietary data and distribution remain scale-constrained.
signal_rationale.transmission: The shift transmits through entry-level hiring, apprenticeship structures, software pricing and valuation, capital allocation, electricity systems, cloud dependence, bargaining power and international distribution of technology rents.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if exposed young-worker hiring recovers while AI adoption rises, seat-based software pricing remains dominant in agentic workflows, generic application margins retain durable premiums, and cloud/compute/energy bottlenecks and concentration fall materially.

en.title: AI is making software and cognitive work more abundant — while concentrating the infrastructure that produces them
en.deck: Falling task and application costs are compressing entry-level work and generic software rents while compute, energy, data, distribution and trusted workflows become scarcer and more strategic.
en.regime: AI is lowering the cost of digital production faster than the physical and institutional inputs required to deploy it at scale.
en.key_risk: Productivity gains may coexist with weaker entry-level career ladders and a larger share of economic rents accruing to infrastructure, distribution and capital owners.

pt-BR.title: A IA está tornando software e trabalho cognitivo mais abundantes — e a infraestrutura que os produz mais concentrada
pt-BR.deck: A queda do custo de tarefas e aplicações pressiona trabalho de entrada e rendas de software genérico enquanto compute, energia, dados, distribuição e workflows confiáveis se tornam mais escassos e estratégicos.
pt-BR.regime: A IA reduz o custo da produção digital mais rápido do que os insumos físicos e institucionais necessários para implantá-la em escala.
pt-BR.key_risk: Ganhos de produtividade podem coexistir com escadas de carreira mais estreitas e maior parcela das rendas econômicas apropriada por donos de infraestrutura, distribuição e capital.
